content: 1. Renal function may deteriorate in elderly or volume-depleted individuals, particularly with high doses of aspirin. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while furosemide decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Both aspirin and garlic enhance anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while gentamicin decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Both aspirin and ginger enhance anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Both aspirin and ginkgo biloba enhance anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Aspirin increases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide through an unknown mechanism, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Caution, monitoring, and therapy adjustments may be necessary. 7. Green tea may enhance the effects of aspirin through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing the risk of bleeding. This is theoretical and may be related to caffeine content. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Griseofulvin decreases aspirin levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Both aspirin and heparin enhance anticoagulation, and either may increase the toxicity of the other. Close monitoring is required, especially in cardiovascular disease patients using low-dose aspirin with anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents. 10. Both aspirin and horse chestnut seed enhance anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Aspirin decreases the effects of hyaluronidase by rendering tissues partially resistant to its action when given in large systemic doses. Patients may require higher doses of hyaluronidase for equivalent effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Aspirin decreases the effects of hydralazine through pharmacodynamic antagonism, as NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin synthesis. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while hydrochlorothiazide decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Aspirin and hydrocortisone may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Ibrutinib increases the effects of aspirin through enhanced anticoagulation, raising the risk of hemorrhage. Patients on antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapies should be closely monitored for bleeding. 16. Both aspirin and ibuprofen enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin may also increase the effects of intravenous ibuprofen by competing for renal tubular clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Aspirin and icosapent may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially prolonging bleeding time. Periodic monitoring is recommended when coadministered with other drugs affecting bleeding. 18. Imatinib and aspirin may increase each other's toxicity. Imatinib can cause thrombocytopenia, increasing bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulants, NSAIDs, platelet inhibitors, or thrombolytic agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 19. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while indapamide decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Both aspirin and indomethacin enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Aspirin increases the effects of various forms of insulin (e.g., aspart, glargine, lispro) through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia when high doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) are used. Insulin dose adjustments and frequent glucose monitoring are necessary. 22. Aspirin and irbesartan both increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin decreases the effects of irbesartan through pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially leading to renal function deterioration, especially in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 23. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while isoproterenol decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Both aspirin and ketoprofen enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Both aspirin and ketorolac (including intranasal forms) enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Both aspirin and labetalol increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin decreases the effects of labetalol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may reduce prostaglandin synthesis. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Aspirin and latanoprost (or latanoprostene bunod ophthalmic) have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Conflicting reports suggest either increased or decreased intraocular pressure (IOP) when ophthalmic prostaglandins are coadministered with NSAIDs. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while levalbuterol decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Aspirin and levomilnacipran may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. SNRIs may further impair platelet activity in patients taking antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Aspirin and lisinopril may increase each other's toxicity, potentially leading to renal function deterioration, particularly with high-dose aspirin in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Aspirin increases lithium levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Both aspirin and lornoxicam enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Both aspirin and losartan increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin decreases the effects of losartan through pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially leading to renal function deterioration, especially in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 34. Both aspirin and meclofenamate enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Both aspirin and mefenamic acid enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Melatonin enhances the effects of aspirin through anticoagulation and may decrease prothrombin time. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 37. Both aspirin and meloxicam enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Aspirin and mesalamine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive nephrotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 39. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while metaproterenol decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Aspirin and methazolamide may increase each other's levels due to inhibition of renal tubular secretion. Methazolamide may also shift salicylates from plasma to the CNS, increasing the risk of neurotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while methyclothiazide decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Aspirin and methylprednisolone may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while metolazone decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Both aspirin and metoprolol increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin decreases the effects of metoprolol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may reduce prostaglandin synthesis. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Aspirin and milnacipran may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 46. Aspirin increases anticoagulation, while mistletoe decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Aspirin and moexipril may increase each other's toxicity, potentially leading to renal function deterioration, particularly with high-dose aspirin in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Aspirin decreases the effects of moxisylyte through pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin synthesis. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Aspirin increases the levels or effects of mycophenolate through competition for renal tubular clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 50. Both aspirin and nabumetone enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 51. Both aspirin and nadolol increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin decreases the effects of nadolol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may reduce prostaglandin synthesis. Caution and monitoring are advised. 52. Aspirin and nafcillin may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition or reduced renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 53. Both aspirin and naproxen enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 54. Both aspirin and nebivolol increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin decreases the effects of nebivolol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may reduce prostaglandin synthesis. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Aspirin and nefazodone may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Aspirin increases anticoagulation, while nettle decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Aspirin and nitazoxanide may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 58. Aspirin increases the effects of nitroglycerin (rectal or sublingual) through additive vasodilation, enhancing vasodilatory and hemodynamic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
